title: Amazon US Black Friday 2024: Top Smartphone Deals Unveiled on GSMArena.com
body:
The countdown to Black Friday is almost over, and Amazon’s week‑long smartphone sale is winding down with some of the deepest price cuts of the season. Shoppers have just a few hours left to snag flagship devices at discounts that rival the best holiday promotions of the past year, while a fresh wave of offers is set to hit the site tomorrow when the official Black Friday rush begins. From premium flagships to budget‑friendly models, the retailer’s lineup showcases a blend of brand‑driven markdowns and carrier‑linked incentives that could reshape the U.S. smartphone market in the weeks ahead.

Amazon’s most eye‑catching deal this week is a $200 reduction on the Samsung Galaxy S23 Ultra, bringing the 256 GB variant down to $899 from its regular $1,099 price tag. The discount not only undercuts most carrier‑offered promotions but also positions the device as a viable alternative to Apple’s iPhone 15 Pro, which remains priced above $1,000 even after carrier subsidies. Analysts note that Samsung’s aggressive pricing could be a strategic move to regain market share lost to Apple’s ecosystem lock‑in, especially as the company pushes its new “Eco‑Mode” power‑saving features to appeal to environmentally conscious consumers.

Apple fans are not left out of the bargain bin. The iPhone 15 and 15 Plus are both listed at $699 for the 128 GB models, a $100 markdown from their standard retail price. While the discount is modest compared to Samsung’s, it is significant given Apple’s historically tight control over pricing. The cut appears to be driven by carrier partners who are willing to absorb a portion of the cost in exchange for new contract sign‑ups, a tactic that could boost Apple’s installed base ahead of the rollout of iOS 18 later this year.

Mid‑range contenders are also seeing substantial price drops. The Google Pixel 8 is offered at $549, $50 off its usual price, and the OnePlus 11 is marked down by $150, landing at $649. These reductions reflect a broader industry trend where manufacturers are using the holiday window to clear inventory ahead of the anticipated release of next‑generation chips and 5G‑only devices slated for early 2027. For consumers, the timing is ideal: the devices provide a near‑flagship experience without the premium price, and many come bundled with accessories such as wireless earbuds or extended warranties.

Carrier‑specific promotions add another layer of complexity to the shopping landscape. T‑Mobile, Verizon, and AT&T each offer additional credits or trade‑in bonuses that can push the effective price of a handset even lower. For example, a Verizon‑linked purchase of the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 5 includes a $250 trade‑in bonus for eligible older devices, effectively reducing the net cost to under $1,000. Such offers incentivize customers to stay within a carrier’s ecosystem, potentially locking them into multi‑year contracts that benefit the carriers’ bottom lines.

The limited‑time nature of these deals is a double‑edged sword. While the discounts are compelling, inventory levels for high‑demand models have already begun to thin out, prompting some shoppers to experience “out‑of‑stock” notifications before they can complete a purchase. Retail analysts warn that the most coveted smartphones—particularly the S23 Ultra and iPhone 15—could sell out within hours of the final Black Friday countdown. This scarcity may drive a secondary market surge, with resellers posting inflated prices on platforms like eBay and StockX, a phenomenon observed in previous holiday seasons.

Looking ahead, the final Black Friday day promises an even broader set of promotions, as Amazon typically unveils “door‑buster” offers that are only available for a few hours. Industry watchers expect deeper cuts on older flagship models, such as the Samsung Galaxy S22 series and the iPhone 14, as retailers aim to clear remaining shelf space before the holiday rush. For consumers, the key will be balancing the urgency of limited‑time deals with the risk of missing out on future price drops. As the holiday shopping season accelerates, the smartphone market will likely see a flurry of activity that could set pricing benchmarks for the next twelve months.
